opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kimberly Dennis (employee ID E010) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E010.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a full_time Payroll Specialist. Requested admin to Source Code. Source Code is owned by Engineer, not Payroll Specialist, so admin is not allowed. Max for full_time without owning role is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Kimberly Dennis (E010) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors can have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested admin to Source Code, which exceeds max of read. Recommend read.
reason: Kimberly Dennis (E010) requested admin access to Source Code. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Kimberly is a Payroll Specialist, so admin is not permitted regardless of employment type. The notes conflict on employment type: one says full_time (max write) and the other says contractor with basic security training (max read, since advanced training is required for write and contractors never get admin). Given the conflicting information, I grant the more restrictive permissible level, read, which matches the Security agent's recommendation and stays within policy under both the contractor interpretation (read is the exact max) and the full_time interpretation (read is below write max but never exceeds the request).
